ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders holding or controlling 25% or more, and ultimate beneficial owners against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, Canada's Special Economic Measures Act (S.C. 1992, c. 17) regulations, the Criminal Code terrorist entity list, OFAC SDN list for USD-denominated wire and letter-of-credit payment rails, and the consolidated Canadian government sanctions schedule. Enhanced due diligence is required for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons and senior public officials under FINTRAC's interpretation of the PCMLTFA. Positive hits require immediate escalation to the designated AML compliance officer, Ministerial approval where applicable, and refusal or conditional on-boarding consistent with Canadian and international trade compliance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: British Columbia Corporate Online Registry (BC Corporate Registry / bcregistry.ca), operated by the Office of the Registrar of Companies under the Ministry of Finance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin characters and include a legal element such as 'Inc.' or 'Corp.'. If an alternate name is to be used in a non-Latin script or through transliteration, the corporate name must first be filed in English or French, and the transliterated form may be recorded as a corporate alias subject to non-confusion assessment. No misleading, obscene, or explicitly prohibited word can form part of the name. Canadian requirements under the federal NLF and BC's name regulation require conformity with ordinary linguistic conventions and avoidance of resemblance to existing registered names or marks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations may be extended on application before expiry, up to a maximum of two additional 56-day periods, by paying the prescribed extension fee and providing a fresh name search report. If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, a written Request for Reconsideration may be delivered to the BC Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the refusal, together with the statutory filing fee, an updated name search/confirmation report, and supporting legal and factual memorandum identifying why the name is not contrary to section 22 of the Business Corporations Act. The Registrar will issue a determinative decision within 15 business days after receipt. No statutory administrative appeal lies beyond such decision; the aggrieved party may apply for judicial review to the Supreme Court of British Columbia.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. The BC Business Corporations Act requires the registered office to be a specific physical street address located in British Columbia and the service address must be a designated place where notices may be personally served. A standalone virtual office, P.O. box, or bare mail-forwarding address is not permissible as the sole registered office. A registered agent offering a virtual office arrangement may be used only where it provides actual office accommodation with a dedicated physical meeting room and fixed street address that the corporation occupies as its registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. For a Class III medical device manufacturer with coronary drug-eluting stent production, the probability of unannounced Health Canada physical inspection is approximately 72% within the first 24 months of licensing, rising to 85% where sterile-lab claims or clinical trial supports are made. BC municipal zoning and fire inspection authorities also retain independent authority to conduct unannounced on-site checks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, ss. 5, 9, 10, 19, 21, 23, 32 and 105; Business Corporations Regulation, BC Reg 164/2004.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry (BC Registry Services), Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia; online filing via Corporate Online.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application together with Notice of Articles; the Registry issues the official Certificate of Incorporation upon success.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act. A private corporation may issue shares for any lawful consideration; no paid-up capital escrow account is mandated for ordinary incorporation. Escrow or capital trust obligations arise only if shares are designed for public listing or regulated capital purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, unanimously, as follows: 1. THAT the subscribers to the incorporation application subscribe for and the board issues to each subscribing director one common share in the Corporation at par value CAD $0.01, receipt of which is acknowledged and credited fully paid. 2. THAT the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at [insert physical address in British Columbia, Canada] and the records office is the office of the corporate secretary, as listed in the Notice of Articles. 3. THAT [CEO name] is appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, [CFO name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, and [Secretary name] is appointed Corporate Secretary, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting or until earlier removal. This resolution being carried, the directors authorize execution of all registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry (BC Registry Services), Corporate Online; NUANS preliminary search under the BC Business Corporations Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an availability search on Corporate Online for the proposed corporate name, including the required 'Inc.', 'Corp.', or 'Ltd.' legal element. File an online name reservation if desired or proceed directly with the incorporation application using the vetted name. Confirm the name does not conflict with federal or provincial trademarks and meets BCBCA distinctiveness requirements.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name
Name reservation application (if filed)
NUANS or Corporate Online name search confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on confusion or distinctiveness grounds, file a substituted name reservation or submission for administrative review with a written explanation; provide evidence of coexistence or corporate identification where appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Incorporation Application and Constating Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry via Corporate Online; authorized electronic filing under BCBCA.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Incorporation Application, Notice of Articles, Articles, and initial directors' consents. Include the physical registered office address in British Columbia, the records office address, share capital structure, authorized share classes, and any unanimous shareholder agreement particulars. Digitally sign the prescribed forms and attach consent to act as director for each first director.
required_dossiers: Incorporation Application (signed)
Notice of Articles
Articles of Incorporation or standard articles election
Consent to Act as Director for each initial director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, correct the flagged fields and resubmit the same draft through Corporate Online within 30 days; if the deficiency relates to director capacity or address validity, replace those particulars and file a revised consent form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Incorporation Application and Pay Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, via the Corporate Online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles to the BC Corporate Registry; pay the incorporated entity filing fee using the secure e-payment rail. Await automated validation and issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation. Download the certified Certificate, Notice of Articles, and filing receipt from Corporate Online for subsequent banking and licensing.
required_dossiers: Corporate Online filing invoice
E-payment transaction receipt
Certificate of Incorporation (issued by BC Corporate Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is refused or status is queried, confirm card/bank clearance and resubmit; if the certificate is not issued within the service standard, escalate through Corporate Online help desk or submit a paper correction via registered mail accompanied by the deficiency letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish Registered Office and Records Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry and the designated registered records office; corporate minute book compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the Notice of Articles records a street-must address in British Columbia as the registered office. Appoint a registered records office that may be the same address; organize the statutory minute book, registers of directors, shareholders, and share transfers. File a Notice of Change of Registered Office if the office moves after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Registered office street address in British Columbia
Registered records office address
Corporate seal or signing authority specimen
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the registered office as non-physical, incomplete, or lacking a corporate custodian, immediately file a Notice of Change of Registered Office with a valid BC street address and obtain landlord or occupancy consent before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Organizational Resolution and Share Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; BC Corporate Registry for share and director records; corporate records office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting and adopt the organizational minutes. Accept the subscribers' share subscription, approve the allotment and issuance of shares, adopt the by-laws, appoint the senior officers, and authorize opening of Canadian and cross-border bank accounts. Enter share subscription payments and share certificate issuances in the share register.
required_dossiers: First board minutes and organizational resolutions
Share subscription agreements and payment evidence
Share register and share certificates
Officer acceptances and director declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If directors resign or refuse consent after filing, call an incorporator or shareholder meeting, appoint replacement directors, and file the prescribed notice with the BC registry; for officer gaps, extend by interim resolutions and file corrected minute excerpts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online; BC Ministry of Finance; BC Corporate Registry annual report obligations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retrieve the federal Business Number from the Certificate of Incorporation or register with CRA. Register for GST/HST, payroll source deductions, and corporate income tax accounts. Register the BC PST account if provincial supply occurs. Initiate corporate banking and credit documentation supporting letters of credit and Swift wire payment rails. Calendar the annual report and annual filing deadlines with BC Registry.
required_dossiers: Business Number confirmation letter
GST/HST and BC PST registration confirmations
Corporate banking and payment rail documentation
Annual corporate report calendar and compliance checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or BC tax registrations are delayed or mismatched, use the CRA Business Window helpline to request expedited linkage under the federal Business Number; correct any legal name or address mismatch with the Certificate of Incorporation and file amended notice with the registry if required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada - Medical Devices Directorate (Medical Device Establishment Licence and Class III Device Licence authority), in coordination with British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy as the environmental co-regulator.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) under the Food and Drugs Act and Medical Devices Regulations; Class III Device Licence for the drug-eluting coronary stent; complementary BC Environmental Management Act discharge permit or registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, Environmental Assessment Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Screening level for a light Class III medical device manufacturing facility; a full Environmental Assessment Certificate is required only if the project triggers the Reviewable Projects Regulation by prescribed activity or effluent thresholds. A site-specific environmental discharge authorization or registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process washwater and any aqueous waste must meet municipal sewer-use or BC effluent limits including pH 6.0–9.0, BOD ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 300 mg/L, and COD within discharge permit ceilings; organic and solvent-based emissions must be controlled below volatile organic compound (VOC) thresholds; any laser-gas and micro-debris effluent must be treated and contained under the Environmental Management Act, with hazardous polymer waste and solvent residue handled through certified manifest and disposal programs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the BC Fire Code and local fire marshal inspection; structural load certification by a professional engineer under the BC Building Code and applicable seismic standards; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety registration including WHMIS, laser safety, chemical storage, and cleanroom emergency protocols; municipal zoning and business licence clearance for a medical device manufacturing operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including its Business Registration Online (BRO) service and CRA My Business Account. British Columbia provincial tax administration is handled by the British Columbia Ministry of Finance through eTaxBC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A corporation must obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) and register the applicable program accounts, including a corporate income tax account (RC) and, where required, a GST/HST account (RT). A resident corporation can generally register through CRA Business Registration Online or by filing the applicable corporate tax return. A non-resident corporation may apply for a BN and program accounts using CRA's prescribed non-resident registration process; it may need to provide incorporation documents, registered-office information, details of Canadian activities, and an authorized representative. GST/HST registration is generally required when the corporation is required to collect tax, including when it carries on business in Canada and makes taxable supplies, subject to statutory exceptions. A separate British Columbia PST registration may be required for taxable sales or leases in the province; registration is available through eTaxBC. A BC incorporation or extra-provincial registration does not itself replace CRA or PST registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Canadian corporation is generally a separate taxpayer and has no US-style check-the-box election to be treated as a partnership or disregarded entity. Canadian-resident corporations are subject to federal and applicable provincial corporate income tax on their taxable income; a non-resident corporation is generally taxable on income from carrying on business in Canada, subject to applicable treaty rules. Limited elections and designations apply to particular transactions or regimes, but they do not generally change the corporation's default entity classification. Hybrid entity characterization in another jurisdiction does not itself alter Canadian tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST), harmonized provincial GST (HST) where applicable, and separate British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST). British Columbia is not an HST province.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For GST/HST, the general small-supplier threshold is CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) made by the person and associated persons, calculated under the statutory rules over a single calendar quarter or the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. The threshold is not a blanket exemption for every non-resident: a person carrying on business in Canada may have to register and collect GST/HST without relying on the small-supplier threshold, subject to applicable exceptions. British Columbia PST has separate rules: the small-seller exemption is generally limited to qualifying sellers with no more than CAD 10,000 in qualifying gross revenue in the relevant period and who meet all statutory conditions; it does not apply to every seller or every supply. Manufacturers and other sellers may have registration obligations independent of that exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no general real-time tax-clearance, mandatory e-invoicing API, or digital-stamping requirement for ordinary GST/HST or BC PST invoices. Invoices and records must contain the information required for the transaction and applicable tax rules, and businesses must retain records for statutory periods and make them available to the relevant authority. Electronic records are permitted subject to applicable recordkeeping requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Qualifying exports of goods may be zero-rated for GST/HST where the statutory export conditions are met, including the applicable requirements concerning delivery or shipment outside Canada and the recipient, use, or other transaction facts. The supplier must retain evidence sufficient to establish export and zero-rating eligibility. Services are not automatically zero-rated merely because the customer is offshore: zero-rating depends on the service category and statutory conditions, including exclusions for specified services and services related to Canadian real property or tangible personal property. A registrant may generally claim input tax credits for eligible GST/HST paid or payable on inputs used in commercial activities, subject to documentation and statutory restrictions. BC PST treatment is separate; export transactions may qualify for an exemption or other treatment only under the applicable PST rules and evidence requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian export declaration and proof of acceptance or reporting where required under the Customs Act and export-reporting rules
Commercial invoice and purchase order or sales contract identifying the goods, buyer, destination, and transaction
Bill of lading, airway bill, courier record, or other carrier documentation evidencing shipment and delivery outside Canada
Proof of export and delivery, such as customs records, carrier tracking, or foreign import documentation, as applicable
Supplier accounting records and tax invoices supporting the reported zero-rated supply
Inward remittance certificate is not a general Canadian statutory requirement for export zero-rating
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada does not impose a general statutory deadline to repatriate export proceeds as a condition of GST/HST zero-rating. CRA may deny zero-rating or input tax credits, assess uncollected tax, interest, and applicable penalties if the supplier cannot substantiate eligibility or has made a false statement or omission. Reassessments are subject to statutory limitation periods, which may be extended in cases such as misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful default, or fraud. Knowing or fraudulent conduct may attract civil penalties and, in serious cases, prosecution under the Excise Tax Act. BC PST assessments, interest, and penalties may also apply where a PST exemption or non-taxable treatment is unsupported.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); monetary authority and lender of last resort. Foreign-exchange administration is not centralized; OSFI supervises bank FX risk, FINTRAC enforces cross-border reporting, and CBSA administers customs/export documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under the Currency Act; no exchange-control approval is required for capital inflows, profit remittance, dividends, or liquidation proceeds. The effective hurdle is tax compliance: Part XIII non-resident withholding tax at 25% (treaty-reduced) plus Enhanced Due Diligence and FINTRAC reporting for wire transfers at or above C$10,000.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed repatriation deadline apply to Canadian export receipts. Exporters may hold foreign currency offshore; Canadian-dollar or foreign-currency transfers exceeding C$10,000 trigger FINTRAC reporting, and foreign-exchange gains remain taxable under the Income Tax Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Trade Finance LC Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium for ancillary settlement, Low for primary treasury clearing. Offshore FinTech EMIs cannot act as Canadian domestic clearing accounts; they require FINTRAC MSB registration and a BC Money Services Business Act licence. They are viable only as secondary pay-out channels for cross-border disbursements, with funds swept to a Tier-1 Canadian bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is legally permissible under OSFI guidance, but a High-Risk_Special_License Class III medical-device manufacturer will attract mandatory enhanced video-KYC with digital identity verification, certified corporate-edit evidence, and a compliance-directed interview; an in-branch director appearance may be unconditionally required at the Vancouver corporate banking centre.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk regulated commodity: Class III coronary drug-eluting stent exports to hospital distributors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL), ISO 13485 certificate, CE-marking and UDI label dossier, executed supply agreements with hospital end-user attestation, HS 9021 commercial invoices, and continuous sanctions/PEP screening results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons (PEPs) among directors or beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified source-of-wealth and source-of-funds files, audited financial statements, professional reference letters, and regulatory approvals demonstrating legitimate clinical-trial and procurement relationships.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque multi-jurisdiction chain of ownership confounding UBO verification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chain-of-ownership diagram, certified corporate extracts from all jurisdictions, BC/Canada registry abstracts, CRA tax residency certificates, and signed beneficiary disclosure consents enabling direct bank confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade velocity inconsistent with the production stage of a new med-tech manufacturer
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling 24-month export forecast, purchase-order library with matching invoices, bills of lading and CBSA customs extracts, EDC financing references, and committed-capital agreements validating the anticipated liquidity cycle.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity is routed via SWIFT MT103 direct credit through a Canadian Tier-1 correspondent; CAD settlement occurs on Payments Canada Lynx (real-time gross settlement). Canadian banks require a declaration of economic purpose and source of funds rather than a government purpose code; the capital contribution is recorded as paid-up capital in CRA books. All wires at or above C$10,000 are reported to FINTRAC.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade uses SWIFT MT103 for open-account supplier payments, irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600; SWIFT MT700/MT707) for imported Nitinol and polymer feedstock under EDC confirmation support, and documentary collections (MT400/MT410) for distributor receivables. CAD clears on Lynx; USD settles through Fedwire or CHIPS correspondents of the Canadian operating bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (up to 24-month tenor) under an ISDA master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) for CNY, INR, and BRL contract settlement where onshore convertibility is restricted
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) aligning non-CAD revenue streams with CAD operating expenses
Vanilla FX options (call/put) to hedge procurement of Nitinol, bioresorbable polymer, and laser micro-machining components
Spot settlement overlay under Bank of Canada liquidity infrastructure, with no surrender or conversion-mandate constraints

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under the Business Corporations Act, s. 252
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after each fiscal year-end; first annual report due within 2 months after registration anniversary or first fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: BC late filing fee of CAD 100; two consecutive years of failure to file permits administrative strike-off by the Registrar

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Transparency Report (ATR) on Individuals with Significant Control, Business Corporations Act, Part 11.1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the BC Annual Report; due within 2 months after each fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 100; strike-off risk after consecutive defaults; officers/directors may incur penalties up to CAD 25,000 for false or omitted material control information

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal and Provincial Corporation Income Tax Return (T2)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance-due payment remitted within 3 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of balance owing plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; additional repeated-filing penalties and interest charged on unpaid amounts

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based revenue or asset threshold under the BC Business Corporations Act; an auditor must be appointed unless all shareholders pass an annual unanimous waiver. A reporting issuer, a company whose Articles require an audit, or one subject to lender covenants must obtain audited financial statements in each applicable fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS mandatory for reporting issuers; private BC companies may prepare statements under Canadian ASPE in accordance with the CPA Canada Handbook. All financial statements must follow Canadian GAAP for CRA corporate tax filing purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, all individuals with significant control must be confirmed and the BC Annual Transparency Report filed with the Registrar within 2 months after fiscal year-end. Any share transfer or control change during the year must be recorded in the company's transparency register within 14 days, with updated details included in the next ATR; if no changes occur, the ATR confirms the existing register remains accurate. The transparency register is not public but must be produced to authorities on demand.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD $8,000–$18,000 per year for a small medical-device manufacturing company requiring audited financial statements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit of 15% for a foreign-controlled Canadian corporation; enhanced accelerated capital cost allowance (CCA) for clean energy and manufacturing/processing equipment; no general statutory tax holiday.
